seo_title: SubDuo – Dual Subtitles for Language Learning (Chrome)
seo_desc: Two subtitle languages at once on Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Disney+ and TED. Look up words, replay lines, save vocabulary. Free Chrome extension.
hero_badge: Free Chrome extension · Prime Video, YouTube, Netflix, Disney+ & TED
hero_h1:
Two languages. One screen.
Learn from every show you watch.
hero_desc: SubDuo shows two subtitle languages at once — the original on top, your language below. Double-click a word to see what it means, replay a line with one key, and keep what you learn in a built-in vocabulary list.
hero_note: Uses the subtitles each site already provides · No account · Subtitles stay in your browser

problem_h2: One language at a time. Pause, rewind, look it up, lose the plot.
problem_p:
Watching in a foreign language usually means choosing between subtitles you can learn from and subtitles you can follow.
SubDuo ends the trade-off: both languages sit on screen together, unknown words are a double-click away, and any line comes back with a single key.
compare_lead: Streaming players show one subtitle language at a time. SubDuo adds a second one — and the tools to learn from it.

demo_h2: Four things you'll use every episode
demo_lead: Screens from the extension, shown in your language.
s1_p: Pick any two of the subtitle tracks the title offers — the original on top, your language below. Drag the subtitles anywhere, scroll over a line to resize it, and right-click to change colors, transparency or blur.
s1_alt: Two subtitle lines on a video: the original language on top and the viewer's language below
s2_h3: Missed a line? Play it again.
s2_p: Press S to repeat the line, A and D to step back and ahead, and Q to pause automatically after each line. Press W to open the transcript in Chrome's side panel — both languages, line by line — and click any row to jump there.
s2_alt: The A, S and D keys on the video, with the transcript in both languages in the side panel
s3_h3: Don't know a word? Double-click it.
s3_p: The video pauses and a card shows the meaning at once, translated on your device by Chrome's built-in translator, with the scene's own line as the example. Alt+drag selects a phrase. Tap “Ask AI” for the meaning in context, the pronunciation and an example sentence.
s3_alt: A word card on the video with its translation, the example line, Ask AI and Save
s4_h3: Saved words come back for review.
s4_p: Every saved word keeps the line it came from. Search and filter your vocabulary list, play the pronunciation, and review with flashcards — the better you know a word, the longer it waits before coming back.
s4_alt: The vocabulary list next to a review flashcard with Forgot, Got it and Easy
flow_lead: No account, no setup screens. Install it and press play.
flow1_p: Install SubDuo from the Chrome Web Store, then play a video on Prime Video, YouTube, Netflix, Disney+ or TED.
flow2_p: Click the SubDuo icon and choose one subtitle language for the top line and one for the bottom. Only tracks the title offers are listed.
flow3_p: Double-click words to look them up, press A, S or D to replay lines, and open your vocabulary list from the popup.
features_lead: Built for people who learn by watching — and want the subtitles out of the way until they need them.
feat1_p: Every track the site provides is detected when the video plays, including YouTube's auto-generated subtitles. Choose one per line, or hide one line.
feat2_p: Double-click or Alt+click a word, or Alt+drag a phrase. Playback pauses and the translation appears on the video, done on your device.
feat3_h3: Ask AI when you want more
feat3_p: The meaning in context, the pronunciation and an example sentence, in your display language. Up to 20 explanations a day, free.
feat4_p: Save words with one click, search them, filter by language and hear them with 🔊. Flashcards space out the words you already know.
feat5_p: A for the previous line, S to repeat, D for the next. Q pauses after every line. Blur one line to test yourself, then point at it to check.
feat6_p: Every line in both languages beside the video. The current line is highlighted; click any row to jump to it. Press W to open it.
feat7_p: Drag to move, scroll to resize a line, arrow keys to nudge, align left, center or right. Right-click for color, transparency and blur per line.
feat8_p: Large subtitles on YouTube, subtle ones on Netflix — settings are saved per site and synced through your Chrome.
feat9_p: Menus, translations and AI explanations use the display language you choose, which can differ from Chrome's language.
safety_h2: Your subtitles stay in your browser.
safety_lead: SubDuo reads the subtitle files each site already sends to your browser and draws them there. The only thing it sends out is a phrase you choose to ask AI about, together with its subtitle line.
safe1_p: Subtitles are parsed and drawn in your browser. Your settings, vocabulary list and viewing history are not sent to the developer. Word translations run on your device with Chrome's built-in translator.
safe2_h3: 📖 Only the phrases you ask about
safe2_p: When you tap “Ask AI”, the selected phrase, its subtitle line and the other line on screen, the language codes and a random device ID (for the daily limit) go to the SubDuo server, which asks OpenAI for the explanation. Your IP address is processed to run the service.
safe3_h3: 🚫 No account, no ads, no analytics
safe3_p: There is nothing to sign up for. The extension contains no advertising and no analytics.
safe4_p: “storage” for settings and vocabulary, “scripting” to reconnect open tabs after updates, “sidePanel” for the transcript, and access to the five supported sites only.
note1: Subtitles are not machine-translated. SubDuo shows only the subtitle languages a title actually offers (on YouTube, auto-generated subtitles included). Translation is used only for the words you look up.
note2: Turn off the site's own subtitles. Otherwise the same line shows twice — SubDuo draws its own two lines.
note3: Netflix lists only some languages. Its player hands out a few subtitle tracks per title, depending on your account — SubDuo can only offer what it receives.
note4: On-device translation needs Chrome 138 or later. Chrome downloads a language pack the first time, and some languages aren't covered — then tap “Ask AI”. AI explanations can be wrong and are limited to 20 a day per device.
note5: It relies on each site's player. If a site changes how it delivers subtitles, detection may stop until SubDuo is updated. Live streams are unverified. Requires desktop Google Chrome 116 or later.
faq1_q: Which sites does SubDuo work on?
faq1_a: Prime Video (primevideo.com and the video pages of Amazon stores), YouTube, Netflix, Disney+ and TED. On other pages the popup tells you the site isn't supported, and SubDuo doesn't run there.
faq2_a: No. Both lines are subtitle tracks the site already provides, so you can only pick languages the title offers. Translation is used only for the words and phrases you look up.
faq3_q: How do I look up a word?
faq3_a: Double-click a word in the subtitles (or Alt+click it), or Alt+drag to select a phrase. Playback pauses and a card shows the on-device translation and the line it came from. Tap “Ask AI” for more, or Save to add it to your vocabulary list.
faq4_q: What do the A, S, D, Q and W keys do?
faq4_a: While SubDuo is showing subtitles, A jumps to the previous line, S repeats the current line, D moves to the next line, Q turns pausing after each line on or off, and W opens the transcript in the side panel.
faq5_q: Is anything sent to a server?
faq5_a: Subtitles, settings and your vocabulary list stay in your browser. Only when you tap “Ask AI” are the selected phrase, its subtitle context, the language codes and a random device ID sent to the SubDuo server, which uses OpenAI to write the explanation. See the privacy policy for details.
faq6_a: Yes. No sign-up and no paid plan. AI explanations are limited to 20 a day per device. A subscription to the streaming service itself is still needed where it requires one.
faq7_q: The subtitles show twice. What's wrong?
faq7_a: The site's own subtitles are still on. Turn them off in the player's subtitle menu — SubDuo draws its own two lines.
faq8_a: Yes. The subtitles live inside the player, so they stay in place and scale with the video in fullscreen.
